subject: science
passage: Most humans see color with three types of light-detecting cells in the eye, whereas mantis shrimp have twelve or more. Scientists once assumed that so many receptor types must allow these animals to distinguish colors with extraordinary precision. When researchers actually tested them, however, mantis shrimp struggled to tell apart colors that humans separate easily. The extra receptors, it now appears, may help the shrimp recognize colors quickly rather than ______.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: Scientists expected the shrimp's many receptors to give "extraordinary precision," but tests showed they "struggled to tell apart colors." The final sentence offers a new explanation: speed instead of precision. The blank must name what the receptors do not provide, so "finely" (with fine precision) fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Quickly rather than swiftly" sets up a contrast between two words that mean the same thing, so the sentence would make no sense.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text is about how precisely the shrimp can tell colors apart, not about how bright or intense the colors look to them.
explanation.C: Correct. The tests showed the shrimp cannot make precise color distinctions, so their receptors seem to support fast recognition instead of fine, detailed discrimination.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Saying the shrimp recognize colors quickly "rather than loosely" would imply that they distinguish colors precisely, which the tests contradict.
